brief: Semiconductors (SOX) have sold off sharply, testing major technical support (trend line, range lows, 200-day moving average) while volatility has spiked from dormant to aggressively bid, though it remains below the panic levels seen in prior semiconductor crashes. The character of that volatility has flipped: during the rally investors bid vol chasing upside, now they bid it, above VIX, scrambling for downside protection instead. Valuations have reset to AI-cycle lows, with the SOX forward P/E down to 16x, raising the question of whether the market has already priced in an earnings outlook worse than the fundamentals support. Goldman notes Korea's electronics sector drove roughly 60% of the country's Q3 GDP growth, with tech exports, machinery investment and semiconductor equipment imports all still rising, arguing the underlying semiconductor economy remains resilient even as equities have cracked. The setup is likened to the dot-com bubble pattern, where history suggests one more bounce before the real damage begins. Conclusion: support holding plus resilient fundamentals argue for a bounce, but the volatility signal means the healing process is not finished, and cheap valuations do not automatically mean the trade is safe.
